greek.forms: Nom: ψυχή, Gen: ψυχῆς, Dat: ψυχῇ, Acc: ψυχήν; Plural — Nom: ψυχαί, Gen: ψυχῶν, Dat: ψυχαῖς, Acc: ψυχάς
greek.etymology: From PIE *bʰes- 'to breathe, blow'. English descendants: Psychology (study of the mind), Psyche (the human soul/mind), Psychiatry (medical treatment of mental disorders), Psychosis (severe mental condition). The root connects breath with life and consciousness.
greek.usage_example: ἡ ψυχὴ ἀθάνατός ἐστι (hay psoo-KHAY ah-THAH-nah-tos ES-ti) — The soul is immortal
greek.did_you_know: Ancient Greeks believed the ψυχή (psoo-KHAY) could leave the body during dreams and travel to distant places. This is why waking someone suddenly was considered dangerous - their soul might not have returned yet, potentially causing madness or death.
